title: Sunny and the Honey Bee | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka follows the sound of a honey bee's hive on a warm night and presses her ear to a hollow gum tree to hear the low gentle hum of ten thousand bees all breathing together. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The hum was coming from the tree.

Sunny stopped on the path and listened. A very low sound — not quite a buzz, more of a deep warm vibration, like the tree itself was humming. She walked toward it slowly, one step at a time.

The tree was an old hollow gum — a large opening in the bark about halfway up, dark inside. The hum was louder here. She could feel it in her chest, gently, if she stood very close.

She pressed her ear carefully against the bark.

The sound was extraordinary.

Not just one bee — thousands of bees, all inside the hollow, all breathing and moving and keeping their warmth together. Ten thousand bees, maybe more. All of them making a sound together that was one sound, smooth and low and alive.

She didn't move.

The hive breathed.

She thought: somewhere inside that hum, ten thousand small things are taking care of each other. Keeping each other warm. Keeping the honey safe. Doing all their small careful jobs through the night.

She pressed a little closer.

The hum moved through the bark into her cheek, into her ear, through her whole body — a gentle living vibration.

She thought: this is what it sounds like, to belong somewhere.

She sat down against the base of the tree.

The hive hummed on above her.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, honey bees. Goodnight, little one.
